items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: no intervener (be-family)
items.passage: In 1904, Sámi activist Elsa Laula Renberg published a pamphlet condemning Swedish policies that permitted settlers to encroach on Sámi land. Laula Renberg ______ also the principal organizer of the first Sámi national assembly, which convened in Trondheim, Norway, in February 1917.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject of the blank is “Laula Renberg,” one person, so the verb must be singular. “Was” is the only singular option, and its past tense fits the events of 1904 and 1917.

A.why_wrong: “Were” is a plural verb and does not agree with the singular subject “Laula Renberg.”

B.why_wrong: “Are” is plural (and present tense); the singular subject “Laula Renberg” needs a singular verb.

D.why_wrong: “Have been” is plural and does not agree with the singular subject “Laula Renberg.”

sources.what: 1904 pamphlet “Inför lif eller död?”: critiques of land-use laws and the encroachment of settlers on Sámi land; the 1917 assembly in Trondheim opened February 6, which she initiated and chaired
Laula Renberg was the main organizer of the first Sámi congress in 1917
1904 polemical pamphlet condemning state support for settlers given land in the north; first pan-Nordic Sámi assembly in Trondheim, February 1917

items.notes: Subject area: history. Cell official median 26 words, 75th percentile 27. Sources differ on her exact role in 1917 (Kvinnemuseet: main organizer; Wikipedia: initiated and chaired the assembly; SKBL: arranged by the Brurskanken women’s association she founded, with her as opening speaker); “principal organizer” follows the first two.
items.rewrite: New subject (Elsa Laula Renberg and the 1917 Sámi assembly) replacing the one-sentence Inge Lehmann item; two sentences with context; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: participial phrase (lexical verb)
items.passage: American composer Gabriela Lena Frank often draws on her mother’s Peruvian heritage. Her string quartet Leyendas: An Andean Walkabout, completed in 2001, ______ the distinctive timbres of traditional Andean instruments, such as panpipes and the tarka, a wooden flute that is blown harshly to split its tone.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is “Her string quartet,” which is singular; the title and the phrase “completed in 2001” only identify and describe it. The singular verb “imitates” agrees with “quartet.”

B.why_wrong: “Imitate” is the plural form and does not agree with the singular subject “quartet.”

C.why_wrong: “Are imitating” is plural and does not agree with “quartet.”

D.why_wrong: “Have imitated” is plural and does not agree with “quartet.”

sources.what: American composer; mother Peruvian (of Chinese descent); her work draws on her mother’s Peruvian heritage and evokes Andean instruments such as the pan flute and charango
Leyendas: An Andean Walkabout, string quartet, 2001; movements depict the panpipe (toyo, zampoña) and the tarka, “a heavy wooden duct flute that is blown harshly in order to split the tone”
Frank is the daughter of a Chinese/Peruvian mother; the piece mixes western classical and Andean folk traditions

items.notes: Subject area: arts. Cell official median 37 words, 75th percentile 44.
items.rewrite: New subject (Gabriela Lena Frank’s Leyendas quartet) replacing the textbook waggle-dance fact; denser register; verb changed to “imitates”.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: missing main verb
items.passage: Labiodental consonants such as “f” and “v” are much rarer in the languages of hunter-gatherers than in those of farming societies. A 2019 study led by linguist Damián Blasi ______ this disparity to softer agricultural diets, which allow the adolescent overbite to persist into adulthood.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The second sentence has a subject, “A 2019 study,” but no main verb unless the blank supplies one; “led by linguist Damián Blasi” only describes the study. “Attributes” is a finite verb that agrees with “study” and completes the sentence.

A.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (-ing)
A.why_wrong: With “attributing,” the sentence has no main verb and becomes a fragment.

B.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (having + past participle)
B.why_wrong: “Having attributed” cannot serve as a main verb, so the sentence is left without one.

C.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (to + base)
C.why_wrong: The infinitive “to attribute” cannot be the main verb of the sentence.

sources.what: Blasi et al. 2019, Science: labiodentals (“f,” “v”) innovated after the Neolithic; diet changes produced a bite that preserves adolescent overbite and overjet into adulthood, favoring labiodentals
Hunter-gatherer languages have about one-fourth the labiodentals of food-producing societies; softer foods of agricultural societies
Study led by linguist Damián Blasi (University of Zurich); hunter-gatherers use about 27 percent of the labiodentals of societies with softer foods

items.notes: Subject area: social science (linguistics). Cell official median 31 words, 75th percentile 32.
items.rewrite: New subject (Blasi 2019, diet and labiodental sounds) replacing the textbook gecko-setae fact; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: second verb of compound predicate
items.passage: Efuru (1966) made Nigerian writer Flora Nwapa the first African woman novelist published in English in Britain. Nwapa later founded Tana Press, an Enugu publishing house aimed at a large female readership, and ______ several of her subsequent novels, among them Women Are Different (1986), under its imprint.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “Nwapa” already has one verb, “founded,” and “and” calls for a second verb in the same form. “Issued” is a finite past-tense verb that pairs with “founded.”

A.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (-ing)
A.why_wrong: “And issuing” does not pair with the finite verb “founded”; the second verb of the predicate must also be finite.

C.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (to + base)
C.why_wrong: “And to issue” is an infinitive and cannot be joined by “and” to the finite verb “founded.”

D.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (having + past participle)
D.why_wrong: “And having issued” is not a finite verb, so it cannot serve as the second verb of “Nwapa.”

sources.what: Efuru (Heinemann, 1966); Nwapa the first African woman novelist published in English in Britain; founded Tana Press, a press targeted at a large female audience, which published her own works such as Women Are Different (1986); Enugu imprint
Women Are Different, Enugu: Tana Press, 1986; Nwapa founded Tana Press herself

items.notes: Subject area: literature. Cell official median 44.5 words, 75th percentile 49.75. Tana Press’s founding year varies by source (1970, 1974, 1976, 1977), so the passage gives none.

fixes: “targeting a predominantly female readership” changed to “aimed at a large female readership,” the wording the source supports (Wikipedia: “targeted at a large female audience”)

items.rewrite: New subject (Flora Nwapa and Tana Press) replacing the Noguchi item that cloned the Gilliam “applied ... and suspended them” frame; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: to-infinitive of purpose
items.passage: From 1573 to 1812, Spanish colonial authorities compelled Indigenous communities within a designated Andean region to supply laborers to silver and mercury mines, a system known as the mita. Economist Melissa Dell used the region’s historical boundary ______ present-day living standards in districts on either side of it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The clause “Economist Melissa Dell used the region’s historical boundary” is already complete. The blank begins a phrase telling why she used the boundary, and the infinitive “to compare” expresses that purpose.

B.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
B.why_wrong: “Compares” is a finite verb with no subject of its own, so it cannot follow the complete clause.

C.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
C.why_wrong: “Compared” would be a second main verb in a clause that already has “used,” with no subject or conjunction.

D.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
D.why_wrong: “Compare” is a finite form with no subject; the sentence needs a phrase stating purpose, not another verb.

sources.what: Dell 2010, Econometrica: the mita, a forced mining labor system in Peru and Bolivia from 1573 to 1812, studied with a regression discontinuity design; lower household consumption today in mita districts
The mita required Indigenous communities within a designated boundary to supply labor to mines; Dell’s design leverages the mita boundary
Mita labor drafts for the Potosí silver mines and the Huancavelica mercury mines

items.notes: Subject area: social science (economics). Cell official median 34 words, 75th percentile 41. Key is the longest option, as in official 1.8.
items.replaced: Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank (duplicate of rhetorical_synthesis.EXAMPLE.easy)
items.rewrite: New subject (Melissa Dell’s mita boundary study) replacing the Momofuku Ando origin anecdote; denser register; options now follow the 1.8 pattern (key the longest).

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: -ing participial phrase
items.passage: Healthy coral reefs crackle with the sounds of snapping shrimp and grunting fish, whereas degraded reefs fall quiet. In a six-week experiment at Australia’s Lizard Island, marine biologist Tim Gordon’s team used underwater loudspeakers to broadcast recordings of healthy reefs on patches of coral rubble, ______ the abundance of fish there.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The words before the comma already form a complete sentence, with the subject “marine biologist Tim Gordon’s team” and the verb “used.” The blank begins a phrase describing the result of the broadcasts, and the participle “doubling” attaches that phrase without adding a second main verb.

A.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
A.why_wrong: “Doubles” is a finite present-tense verb with no subject, which leaves the sentence ungrammatical.

B.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
B.why_wrong: “Had doubled” is a finite verb with no subject of its own, so it cannot follow the comma and the complete clause.

D.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
D.why_wrong: “Doubled” would be a second past-tense verb with no subject or conjunction after a complete sentence.

sources.what: Gordon et al. 2019, Nature Communications: six-week field experiment; loudspeaker playback of healthy reef sound on coral-rubble patch reefs; a doubling in overall fish abundance
Study site: the lagoon south-west of Lizard Island Research Station, northern Great Barrier Reef; 40 days of playback in late 2017
Healthy reefs: the crackle of snapping shrimp and the whoops and grunts of fish; degraded reefs become quiet; lead author Tim Gordon

items.notes: Subject area: science. Cell official median 47 words, 75th percentile 47. Distractor set follows official 2.9 (finite forms after a complete clause), not the comma-splice set.

fixes: “Tim Gordon and colleagues” changed to “Tim Gordon’s team” (six items of the skill opened with “X and colleagues”)
options reordered so the set no longer repeats the official 2.9 order (earned / had earned / earning / earn); key stays C

items.rewrite: New subject (Tim Gordon’s reef-sound playback experiment) replacing the famous Mansa Musa anecdote; finite-form distractors instead of comma splices; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Tense: simple present (general)
items.passage: Biologists Aaron Corcoran and William Conner have documented that Mexican free-tailed bats sabotage one another’s echolocation. As a hunting bat approaches an insect, its calls accelerate into a rapid “feeding buzz.” A competitor that detects this buzz ______ a jamming signal that sweeps through the frequencies the hunter relies on, frequently causing it to miss.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The passage describes what these bats regularly do, in the present tense: a hunting bat “approaches,” its calls “accelerate,” and a competitor “detects” the buzz. The simple present “emits” keeps the sentence in that time frame.

A.recipe: Simple past where present is needed
A.why_wrong: “Emitted” is past tense and clashes with the present-tense “detects” in the same sentence.

B.recipe: Past perfect where the cue is present
B.why_wrong: “Had emitted” places the action before another past event, but the passage describes a recurring present behavior.

C.why_wrong: “Would have emitted” describes something that did not happen, which does not fit a description of what the bats actually do.

sources.what: Corcoran and Conner, Science 2014: Mexican free-tailed bats make a jamming call during another bat’s feeding buzz, the accelerating calls of the final second of an attack; the call cuts capture success by about 70 percent
Conner: the call “sweeps through the frequency range that bats use”; produced only when another bat was homing in on a moth; bats hearing it were far more likely to miss

items.notes: Subject area: science. Cell official median 44 words, 75th percentile 48.
items.rewrite: New subject (Corcoran and Conner on bats jamming rivals’ sonar) replacing the textbook Venus flytrap fact; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Tense: simple past (dated)
items.passage: Hoag-type galaxies, which consist of a round core encircled by a ring of stars with no visible connection between them, constitute less than 0.1 percent of observed galaxies. In 2017, Turkish American astrophysicist Burçin Mutlu-Pakdil and colleagues ______ that one such galaxy, PGC 1000714, also displays evidence of a second, diffuse inner ring.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The phrase “In 2017” places the researchers’ report at a specific time in the past, so the simple past “reported” is needed.

A.recipe: Present simple where another tense is needed
A.why_wrong: “Report” is present tense, but the report was made in 2017.

C.why_wrong: “Will report” points to the future and contradicts “In 2017.”

D.recipe: Present perfect where another tense is needed
D.why_wrong: “Have reported” is not used with a specific past time such as “In 2017.”

sources.what: Hoag-type galaxies: a round core surrounded by a circular ring with nothing visibly connecting them; “Less than 0.1% of all observed galaxies are Hoag-type”; PGC 1000714 shows evidence of a second, diffuse inner ring; study published January 2017 in MNRAS
Mutlu-Pakdil et al., MNRAS 466 (2017): photometric study of PGC 1000714, two fairly round rings
Burçin Mutlu-Pakdil, Turkish American astrophysicist

items.notes: Subject area: science. Cell official median 37.5 words, 75th percentile 37.75.
items.rewrite: New subject (Mutlu-Pakdil’s double-ringed Hoag-type galaxy) replacing the textbook Hangul fact; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Tense: past perfect (earlier past)
items.passage: In 1982, a sponge diver from the Turkish village of Yalıkavak described seeing “metal biscuits with ears” on the seafloor off Uluburun, a cape near Kaş. From his sketches, archaeologists recognized the objects as copper oxhide ingots, cargo from a merchant vessel that ______ there more than three thousand years earlier.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The 1982 report is itself in the past, and “more than three thousand years earlier” places the ship’s loss before it. The past perfect “had sunk” shows an action completed before another past moment.

A.recipe: Present simple where another tense is needed
A.why_wrong: “Sinks” is present tense, but the ship went down thousands of years ago.

B.why_wrong: “Will sink” points to the future and contradicts “more than three thousand years earlier.”

D.why_wrong: “Is sinking” describes something happening now, not an event completed millennia before 1982.

sources.what: Found in summer 1982 by Mehmed Çakir, a sponge diver from Yalıkavak, whose sketches of “metal biscuits with ears” were recognized as oxhide ingots; off Uluburun about 9.7 km southeast of Kaş; wreck dated to the late 14th century BC; about 10 tons of copper

items.notes: Subject area: history (archaeology). Cell official median 40 words, 75th percentile 45.5. No simple-past distractor, since “sank” would also be acceptable.

fixes: “reported seeing” changed to “described seeing” to cut the “reported” lead-in repeated across the skill

items.rewrite: New subject (the 1982 discovery of the Uluburun wreck) replacing the well-worn Gutenberg and Bi Sheng contrast; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: appositive (with plural nouns)
items.passage: Iranian poet Forugh Farrokhzad directed only one film, The House Is Black (1962), which was shot in a leprosy colony. The documentary, a portrait of the colony’s residents set to readings from scripture and Farrokhzad’s own poems, ______ now widely considered a precursor of the Iranian New Wave.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject of the second sentence is “The documentary,” which is singular. The phrase between the commas renames it, and its plural nouns (“residents,” “readings,” “poems”) do not change the subject’s number, so the singular “is” is correct.

B.why_wrong: “Are” agrees with the nearby plurals “readings” and “poems,” not with the singular subject “The documentary.”

C.why_wrong: “Have been” is plural and does not agree with the singular subject “The documentary.”

D.why_wrong: “Were” is plural and does not agree with “The documentary.”

sources.what: The House Is Black (1962), the only film by the poet Forugh Farrokhzad, set in an Iranian leper colony and accompanied by passages from the Old Testament, the Koran and her own poems
Footage from the Bababaghi leper colony; narration spliced with the Old Testament, the Qur’an and her poetry; it “paved the way for the Iranian New Wave”
The film “paved the way for the country’s New Wave”

items.notes: Subject area: arts (film). Cell official median 40.5 words, 75th percentile 47.25. Replaces an earlier draft subject (Lienzo de Quauhquechollan) that was too close to inferences.S9.medium.
items.replaced: Jacob Lawrence, The Migration Series (duplicate of inferences.S9.easy)
items.rewrite: New subject (Forugh Farrokhzad’s The House Is Black) replacing the famous Book of Kells; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: prepositional phrase
items.passage: Using 22 billion position messages that ships broadcast to avoid collisions, researchers led by David Kroodsma of Global Fishing Watch mapped the activity of more than 70,000 fishing vessels from 2012 to 2016. Their analysis of these vessels’ routes ______ that industrial fishing occurs in more than 55 percent of the ocean’s area.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is “Their analysis,” which is singular; “of these vessels’ routes” only tells what was analyzed. The singular verb “indicates” agrees with “analysis.”

A.why_wrong: “Indicate” agrees with the nearby plural “routes,” not with the singular subject “analysis.”

B.why_wrong: “Are indicating” is plural and does not agree with “analysis.”

C.why_wrong: “Have indicated” is plural and does not agree with “analysis.”

sources.what: Kroodsma et al. 2018, Science: 22 billion AIS messages, more than 70,000 industrial fishing vessels tracked from 2012 to 2016; industrial fishing occurs in more than 55% of ocean area
AIS was originally designed to help prevent ship collisions by broadcasting a ship’s identity, position, speed and turning angle
Kroodsma affiliated with Global Fishing Watch; 22 billion AIS messages; >70,000 industrial fishing vessels, 2012 to 2016; fishing in >55% of ocean area (abstract)

items.notes: Subject area: science. Cell official median 41 words, 75th percentile 47.5.

fixes: “researcher David Kroodsma and colleagues” changed to “researchers led by David Kroodsma of Global Fishing Watch” (stock “and colleagues” opener, used in six items of the skill); affiliation sourced

items.rewrite: New subject (Kroodsma 2018, global footprint of fishing from ship tracking) replacing the textbook Omori aftershock law; denser register.

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: compound subject with “and”
items.passage: In 2016, the Lima campus of the Peruvian engineering university UTEC received the inaugural RIBA International Prize, whose jury likened the building to a “modern-day Machu Picchu.” Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara, whose Dublin firm, Grafton Architects, designed the campus, ______ named the 2020 laureates of the Pritzker Architecture Prize.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is two people joined by “and,” Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara, so it is plural. The clause about their firm only describes them, so the plural “were” is correct.

A.why_wrong: “Was” is singular and seems to agree with the nearby “firm” or “campus,” but the subject is the plural “Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara.”

C.why_wrong: “Has been” is singular and does not agree with the compound subject.

D.why_wrong: “Is” is singular and does not agree with the compound subject.

sources.what: Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara of Grafton Architects, Dublin, are the 2020 Pritzker laureates; University Campus UTEC Lima was awarded the inaugural RIBA International Prize 2016
Jury described the UTEC campus as a “modern day Machu Picchu”; inaugural RIBA International Prize

items.notes: Subject area: arts (architecture). Cell official median 38.5 words, 75th percentile 46.25.
items.rewrite: New subject (Grafton Architects, UTEC campus and the 2020 Pritzker) replacing the famous Hedy Lamarr patent and its planted “pair” appositive; denser register; re-lettered.

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: relative pronoun “that” (antecedent is an appositive noun after plural nouns)
items.passage: For the first Chicago Architecture Biennial in 2015, Mexican architect Tatiana Bilbao built a full-scale prototype of a house for low-income families. Its rigid core of concrete blocks is surrounded by lightweight modules made of wooden pallets, a combination that ______ residents to expand the dwelling in phases while its exterior always looks finished.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The relative pronoun “that” refers to “a combination,” the noun right before it, not to the plural “pallets,” “modules,” or “blocks.” Because “combination” is singular, the verb in the “that” clause must be singular, and “allows” is the only singular option.

A.why_wrong: “Allow” is plural, as if “that” referred to “pallets” or “modules,” but it refers to the singular “combination.”

C.why_wrong: “Are allowing” is plural and does not agree with “combination.”

D.why_wrong: “Have allowed” is plural and does not agree with “combination.”

sources.what: Full-scale prototype at the Chicago Architecture Biennial; program for people with very low salaries; residents wanted a house that looks like a house rather than an unfinished one with exposed rebar; house can grow as the family grows

Presented at the inaugural Chicago Architecture Biennial (2015); prototype erected inside the city’s cultural center; central core of rigid concrete blocks surrounded by modules of wooden pallets; expanded in phases while preserving the home’s external appearance

items.notes: Subject area: arts (architecture). Cell official median 36 words.
items.rewrite: Replaced Niemeyer’s National Congress (tidy single-sentence “which” frame) with Tatiana Bilbao’s 2015 Biennial housing prototype; “that” clause after an appositive noun with plural attractors.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: verb of a “that” clause split by a relative clause
items.passage: Tambaqui, large fruit-eating fish of the Amazon basin, forage in seasonally flooded forests. Combining radiotelemetry of wild fish in Peru’s Pacaya-Samiria National Reserve with feeding trials in captivity, ecologist Jill Anderson estimated in 2011 that tambaqui, which can retain ingested seeds for several days, ______ some seeds as far as 5.5 kilometers from the parent plant.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The clause beginning with “that” has the subject “tambaqui” and needs its own finite verb; the relative clause set off by commas only describes the fish. “Disperse” supplies that verb: the fish disperse some seeds as far as 5.5 kilometers.

A.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (-ing)
A.why_wrong: With “dispersing,” the clause beginning “that tambaqui” has no main verb.

B.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (to + base)
B.why_wrong: “To disperse” is an infinitive, so the “that” clause is left without a finite verb.

C.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (having + past participle)
C.why_wrong: “Having dispersed” is a participle and cannot serve as the verb of the “that” clause.

sources.what: Anderson, Nuttle, Saldaña Rojas, Pendergast and Flecker 2011, Proc. R. Soc. B 278: Colossoma macropomum (tambaqui), radiotelemetry in Pacaya-Samiria National Reserve, Peru; gut retention trials with captive fish (seeds retained up to 212 h); modelled maximum dispersal 5495 m, among the longest ever reported; Anderson, ecologist (Cornell, Duke)
Fruit-eating fish of Amazon floodplain forests carry seeds up to 5.5 km

items.notes: Subject area: science. Cell official median 46 words.
items.rewrite: Replaced Karikó and Weissman (compound-predicate clone) with a 2011 tambaqui seed-dispersal study; the blank is now the verb of a “that” clause split by a relative clause.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: -ing participial phrase (result after a complete clause)
items.passage: In the 1890s, gold miners working a peat bog in Russia’s Ural Mountains unearthed fragments of the Shigir Idol, a towering larch sculpture carved with human faces. In 2018, a German-Russian research team radiocarbon-dated the wood to roughly 11,500 years ago, ______ the sculpture’s creation about two thousand years earlier than previous estimates.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The words before the blank already form a complete sentence: the subject “a German-Russian research team” with the verb “radiocarbon-dated.” The participle “placing” begins a phrase that states the result of that dating without adding a second main verb.

B.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
B.why_wrong: “Placed” would be a second main verb attached to a complete clause with only a comma.

C.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
C.why_wrong: “Had placed” is a finite verb with no subject or conjunction joining it to the complete clause.

D.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
D.why_wrong: “Places” is a finite present-tense verb, so the sentence would join two main verbs with only a comma.

sources.what: Found in the Shigir peat bog on the eastern slope of the Middle Urals (24 January 1890); larch wood; extracted in ten parts; several faces carved along it; 1990s radiocarbon date of about 9,500 years; later German analysis about 11,500 years

University of Göttingen press release, 30 April 2018: German-Russian team, systematic radiocarbon dating, age approximately 11,500 years, oldest known wooden sculpture; discovered by gold miners in the Shigir Moor (1894)
Zhilin, Savchenko, Hansen, Heussner and Terberger 2018, Early art in the Urals: new research on the wooden sculpture from Shigir, Antiquity 92

items.notes: Subject area: history (archaeology). Discovery year is 1890 in Wikipedia and 1894 in the Göttingen release, so the passage says “in the 1890s.” Cell official median 50 words.
items.rewrite: Replaced Gabriela Mistral (loose biographical opener) with the 2018 redating of the Shigir Idol; result participle “placing” after a complete clause.

items.subtype: Tense: simple past (dated)
items.passage: Because most folktales circulated orally for centuries before being transcribed, their ages are difficult to estimate. In a 2016 study, Sara Graça da Silva and anthropologist Jamshid Tehrani mapped 275 magic tales onto a phylogeny of Indo-European languages and ______ one tale, “The Smith and the Devil,” back to the Bronze Age, long before the emergence of the literary record.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The phrase “In a 2016 study” places the work at a specific, finished time in the past, and the blank is the second verb in a predicate whose first verb, “mapped,” is in the simple past. The simple past “traced” fits both cues.

A.why_wrong: “Will trace” places the findings of a 2016 study in the future and does not match the past-tense “mapped.”

B.recipe: Present simple or present perfect where another tense is needed
B.why_wrong: The present perfect “have traced” is not used with a specific past time such as “in a 2016 study,” and it breaks the parallel with “mapped.”

D.why_wrong: “Are tracing” describes an action in progress now, not part of a study completed in 2016.

sources.what: da Silva and Tehrani 2016, Royal Society Open Science: comparative phylogenetic methods applied to Indo-European folktales; “The Smith and the Devil” traced back to the Bronze Age; tales originated long before the literary record

Studied 275 magic-based stories; family trees of Indo-European languages; Smith and the Devil about 6,000 years old, Bronze Age; Tehrani an anthropologist at Durham, da Silva at the New University of Lisbon

da Silva and Tehrani 2016 abstract: comparative phylogenetic methods; oral traditions probably originated long before the literary record; “The Smith and the Devil” can be traced back to the Bronze Age

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: long stacked interveners (appositive and prepositional phrases with plural nouns)
items.passage: Sediments from El Salt, a Neanderthal occupation site in southeastern Spain dating to roughly 50,000 years ago, contain what Ainara Sistiaga’s team identified in 2014 as the oldest known human fecal biomarkers. Detection of 5β-stigmastanol, a compound that intestinal bacteria produce from plant sterols, in the earliest of the five samples ______ interpreted as evidence that Neanderthals supplemented meat with plant foods.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject of the second sentence is “Detection,” which is singular. The appositive about the compound and the phrase “in the earliest of the five samples” only describe it, so the plural nouns “bacteria,” “sterols,” and “samples” do not change its number, and the singular “was” is needed.

A.why_wrong: “Were” agrees with the nearby plural “samples” or “sterols,” not with the singular subject “Detection.”

B.why_wrong: “Are” is plural and does not agree with “Detection.”

C.why_wrong: “Have been” is plural and does not agree with “Detection.”

sources.what: Sistiaga, Mallol, Galván and Summons 2014, PLoS ONE 9(6): e101045: five sediment samples from El Salt (Alicante, Spain), Middle Palaeolithic, ca. 50,000 yr BP; oldest positive identification of human faecal matter; 5β-stigmastanol, a microbial product of plant sterols, significant in the oldest sample; evidence of meat and plant intake
full text: 5β-stigmastanol found in the oldest sample (WL H44) of five, pointing to plant intake alongside a meat-dominated diet

C.why_wrong: “Are supporting” is plural and does not agree with “The discovery.”

D.why_wrong: “Have supported” is plural and does not agree with “The discovery.”

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: compound subject (“X and Y”) whose second part ends in singular nouns
items.passage: Geneticist Melissa Ilardo used portable ultrasound to compare the spleens of the Bajau, Indonesian “sea nomads” renowned for breath-hold diving, with those of the Saluan, their land-dwelling neighbors. The roughly 50 percent greater size of Bajau spleens and the prevalence among the Bajau of a PDE10A variant associated with spleen enlargement ______ a genetic adaptation to prolonged diving.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject of the second sentence is compound: “The roughly 50 percent greater size ... and the prevalence ...” Two subjects joined by “and” take a plural verb, so “suggest” is correct even though the nouns closest to the blank, “variant” and “enlargement,” are singular.

A.why_wrong: “Suggests” is singular, as if the subject were only “prevalence” or the nearby “enlargement,” but “size ... and the prevalence” is a plural compound subject.

C.why_wrong: “Is suggesting” is singular and does not agree with the compound subject joined by “and.”

D.why_wrong: “Has suggested” is singular and does not agree with the compound subject joined by “and.”

items.subtype: Subject-verb agreement: possessive inside subject, number differs from head (plus singular “whose” clause)
items.passage: Some scholars long dismissed the Grolier Codex, a Maya manuscript first exhibited in 1971, as a forgery, partly because looters rather than archaeologists had recovered it. Yet the codex’s ten surviving bark-paper pages, whose painted almanac tracks the cycles of Venus, ______ to the thirteenth century, a radiocarbon result that Michael Coe and his coauthors cited in 2016 as evidence of authenticity.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The head of the subject is “pages,” which is plural; “the codex’s” only names the owner of the pages, and the “whose” clause describes them. The plural “date” agrees with “pages.”

A.why_wrong: “Dates” is singular, agreeing with “codex’s” or “almanac” rather than with the plural head noun “pages.”

B.why_wrong: “Has dated” is singular and does not agree with “pages.”

D.why_wrong: “Is dating” is singular and does not agree with “pages.”

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: missing main verb (after a relative clause with its own verb)
items.passage: Since 2005, Bolivian civil engineer Freddy Mamani has transformed the skyline of El Alto with dozens of flamboyant multistory buildings. These structures, which typically combine ground-floor shops, a second-floor event hall, and apartments above, ______ their geometric patterns and vivid colors from the aguayo, the bright woven cloth of the Aymara people.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “These structures” still needs its main verb: “combine” belongs to the “which” clause set off by commas. “Draw” is the only finite verb and completes the sentence.

B.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (-ing)
B.why_wrong: With “drawing,” the subject “These structures” never gets a main verb; “combine” belongs to the “which” clause.

C.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (to + base)
C.why_wrong: “To draw” is an infinitive, so the sentence has no main verb.

D.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (having + past participle)
D.why_wrong: “Having drawn” is a participle, not a main verb, so the sentence is a fragment.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: verb of a “that” clause split by an appositive with its own relative clause
items.passage: When Antarctic krill were fed algae mixed with polyethylene microbeads in a 2018 laboratory study, plastic particles recovered from their bodies were, on average, 78 percent smaller than the original beads. Amanda Dawson, the study’s lead author, proposed that the gastric mill, a structure in the krill’s stomach that ordinarily grinds food particles, ______ ingested beads into fragments, some less than a micrometer wide.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The clause beginning “that the gastric mill” needs its own finite verb; the words between the commas only describe the gastric mill, and “grinds” belongs to that description. “Breaks” supplies the verb of the “that” clause.

A.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (-ing)
A.why_wrong: With “breaking,” the clause beginning “that the gastric mill” has no verb of its own.

B.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (to + base)
B.why_wrong: “To break” is an infinitive, so the “that” clause is left without a finite verb.

D.recipe: Nonfinite where a finite verb is needed (having + past participle)
D.why_wrong: “Having broken” is a participle and cannot be the verb of the “that” clause.

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: to-infinitive of purpose after a compound predicate
items.passage: Mashpee Wampanoag scholar Jessie Little Doe Baird—a former student of linguist Kenneth Hale—analyzed and then catalogued the vocabulary of documents written in Wôpanâak by her colonial-era ancestors ______ a dictionary of more than 10,000 words for a language that had not been spoken for about a century.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence already has its subject, Baird, and its verbs, “analyzed and then catalogued.” The blank begins a phrase explaining why she did this work, and the infinitive “to compile” expresses that purpose.

A.recipe: Wrong nonfinite (participle instead of purpose infinitive)
A.why_wrong: With no comma before it, “compiling a dictionary” attaches to the nearest noun, “ancestors,” so the sentence would say her colonial-era ancestors were compiling a dictionary for a language that had not been spoken for a century. It also fails to state the purpose of Baird’s work.

B.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
B.why_wrong: “Compiled” adds a second main verb with no conjunction after the complete clause “Baird ... analyzed and then catalogued the vocabulary,” so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

C.why_wrong: “And compiling” is not parallel with the finite verbs “analyzed” and “catalogued.”

Language went out of use in the late 19th century; revitalization began 1993; first native speakers in more than a century
Baird drew on Wôpanâak documents written by her ancestors in the 17th and 18th centuries; dictionary of about 11,000 words

items.subtype: Finite vs nonfinite: -ing participial phrase (interrupter between subject and verb)
items.passage: In January 2015, following protests over his novel Madhorubagan, Tamil writer Perumal Murugan publicly declared his own literary death. The Madras High Court, ______ petitions seeking criminal proceedings against the novelist, concluded its 2016 judgment with a one-word sentence addressed to him: “Write.”
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb of the second sentence is “concluded,” and the words between the commas interrupt the subject “The Madras High Court” and that verb. The interrupter must be a modifier, not a second main verb, so the participle “dismissing” is correct.

A.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
A.why_wrong: “Dismissed” makes the interrupter a second main verb for “The Madras High Court,” which clashes with “concluded.”

C.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
C.why_wrong: “Dismisses” is a finite verb, giving the subject two unconnected verbs.

D.recipe: Finite where a nonfinite phrase is needed
D.why_wrong: “Was dismissing” is a finite verb phrase and cannot sit between the subject and “concluded” without a conjunction.

sources.what: Madhorubagan (2010, Tamil; One Part Woman); January 2015 Facebook post “Perumal Murugan the writer is dead”; 5 July 2016 Madras High Court ruling

items.subtype: Tense: past perfect (earlier past, “at the time of”)
items.passage: Senegalese novelist Mohamed Mbougar Sarr received the 2021 Prix Goncourt for The Most Secret Memory of Men, a novel chronicling a young writer’s search for a vanished author. When he won it, Sarr ______ three other novels, among them De purs hommes (2018), an examination of the prejudice and violence surrounding homosexuality in Senegal.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “When he won it” refers to the 2021 award, a moment in the past, and the three novels were published before that moment (one of them in 2018). The past perfect “had published” shows an action completed before another past moment.

B.recipe: Present simple or present perfect where another tense is needed
B.why_wrong: “Has published” is present perfect, which does not fit a moment in the past (“when he won it”).

C.recipe: Present simple or present perfect where another tense is needed
C.why_wrong: “Publishes” is present tense and clashes with the 2021 award and the 2018 novel.

D.why_wrong: “Is publishing” presents an action going on now, not novels already published before the 2021 award.
